key_insight: CS3F shows that frozen 2D foundation models can be repurposed, without training, to localize anomalies in 3D medical volumes by comparing slice-derived volumetric tokens across subjects.
clinical_relevance: This could help flag unusual lesions in MRI and CT when labeled 3D training data are limited or when scanners and patient populations vary.
method: Decompose each 3D scan along multiple anatomical axes and encode slices with a 2D vision transformer.
Pool neighboring slice features into localized volumetric tokens for cross-subject matching.
Use coarse-to-fine tokenization to improve sensitivity to small focal lesions without exhaustive comparison.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports evaluation on brain MRI for metastases, glioma, and stroke, plus validation on lung CT to assess generalizability beyond atlas-aligned brain imaging.
watch_item: Performance may depend strongly on lesion contrast and modality, so fine tokenization may not help equally across all cases.
paper_title: Toward Training-Free Zero-Shot Anomaly Detection in 3D Medical Images: A Batch-Based Approach Using 2D Foundation Models
